open_questions: When was lisinopril first prescribed, and at what dose?
When was the dry cough first documented as a side effect of lisinopril?
Was losartan previously trialed or contraindicated before this initiation?
What blood pressure readings supported continuing lisinopril in June, and were they repeated after switching to losartan?
Was there documentation of renal function or potassium monitoring before stopping lisinopril and starting losartan?
Was the lisinopril stop action confirmed in a subsequent note or order after August 12?

citation.quote: Stop lisinopril because of a dry cough. Start losartan 50 mg daily.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: ACE inhibitor discontinuation due to cough requires confirmation of symptom resolution and monitoring for rebound hypertension or hyperkalemia after switching to ARB.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Confirm dry cough resolved post-lisinopril; check serum potassium and creatinine within 1–2 weeks of losartan initiation.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Unresolved medication conflict may lead to inadvertent re-initiation or omission of lisinopril.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Clarify and reconcile lisinopril status in the medication list and confirm discontinuation in orders and patient education.
